Sugarcane bagasse, a by-product of sugar industries, is an abundant and low-cost biomass source that can be converted into carbon materials through carbonization. This process not only recycles agri- cultural waste but also reduces the environmental impact associated with conventional carbon production methods [24, 25]. Biomass-derived carbon materials offer several advantages over traditional carbon sources. First, they are derived from bio-waste, which contributes to sustainability and reduces material cost [26]. Second, the synthesis process allows morphology engineering like pore size and surface functionalisation to maximize device charge storage capac- ity. Furthermore, grass-derived biochar has been shown to deliver outstanding electrochemical performance due to its high graphitic content and tunable porosity [32]. The renew- able and cost-effective nature of biomass-derived carbons makes them highly attractive for sustainable energy stor - age applications in supercapacitors [ 28, 32]. These devices rely on highly porous materials for electrodes providing a substantial surface area per mass, such as highly porous carbon. Developing high-performance porous carbon from biomass wastes such as waste-activated sludge and spent coffee is a sustainable way to reduce adverse environmental effects, contributing toward a carbon circular economy. In this study, hierarchically porous carbon with a high surface area of 1198 ± 60 m 2 g −1 was synthesized through a green route. Sodium acetate was utilized as an environmentally friendly electrolyte. The long-term stability test at a high current density was conducted, providing valuable insights into the viability of sodium acetate as a robust electrolyte in supercapacitor application. The supercapacitor demonstrated an excellent cycle stability of 98.4% after 20,000 cycles at a current density of 10 A g −1 in sodium acetate. Further assessment revealed dominant fast surface kinetics. Moreover, a maximum energy density of 15.9 Wh kg −1 at 0.2 A g −1 was achieved. By utilizing highly porous carbon in conjunction with a water-based binder, a substantial improvement of 76% in capacity with respect to a nonaqueous-based binder was demonstrated. 1. Hence, they are applicable in electric vehicles (EVs), uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), and hybrid buses. 2 The most common type of supercapacitor is an electrochemical double-layer capacitor (EDLC). In this study, a green, facile, and scalable route of production of activated carbon from WAS and SC waste was developed by using sodium thiosulfate, potassium carbonate, and trisodium citrate as the green activation agents. Notably, no prior studies have explored the synthesis of porous carbon from mixtures of WAS and SC waste using these specified chemicals. CONCLUSIONS In this study, highly porous activated carbon was developed from a sustainable, green route by utilizing eco-friendly activation agents such as sodium thiosulfate, potassium carbonate, trisodium citrate, and inert molten salt (potassium chloride). The effect of activation agents, temperature, mixing procedure, and molten

friendly electrolyte was evaluated for the first time in the long cycle life test. The sodium acetate electrolyte enabled the supercapacitor to operate at a wider operating potential (1.5 V), which results in a higher energy density compared to the traditional aqueous electrolyte (6 M KOH). The electrode maintained an excellent cycle stability of 98.4 ± 0.3% at 10 A g −1 . Future investigation into the binder composition, the activation agent ratio to the carbon precursor, and the mixing ratio of the biomass precursors on the electrochemical performance of the super- capacitor is recommended. Optimization of the yield for the activated carbon material is recommended for future work. Karanikolos* ACCESS | Metrics & More | Article Recommendations | ABSTRACT: Activated carbon (AC) materials were developed via a single-step method from three different biowaste sources and tailored for application in carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) capture and electrochemical energy storage, combining the concept of biowaste valorisation wit

, as well as characteristics and performance. The developed AC materials demonstrated properties such as high graphitization, favorable pore-structure configuration and surface area, and favorable surface characteristics. CO 2 adsorption experiments at 298 K showed a capacity of 2.55 mmol/g at 1 bar with stability over multiple cycles for AC2, as well as high CO 2 / N 2 selectivity, reaching 48 at 1 bar (ideal adsorbed solution theory (IAST)) for a 15:85 v/v CO 2 /N 2 mixture for AC1, suggesting a high selective affinity for CO 2 capture at ambient conditions. Furthermore, electrochemical experiments revealed stable performance as electric double-layer capacitors as a result of low solution and charge-transfer resistance, demonstrating capacitive performance in the order of 250 F/g at a scan rate of 5 mV/s for AC3, which was tested at different increasing scan rates and det

an rate of 100 mV/s. Galvanostatic charge−discharge (GCD) investigations revealed virtually symmetric charge−discharge curves with an acceptable rate capability for a symmetric AC3 full cell, retaining ∼70% of initial capacitance despite a 4-fold increase in current density, and preserving ∼78% of initial capacitance after 1000 cycles. These results reveal the potential of agro-industrial waste streams- derived AC materials for selective carbon capture and electrochemical energy storage, enabling them a simple, potentially scalable, and sustainable material platform for such applications. The key contribution is the processing of three previously underutilized agro-food industrial biomass wastes into functional AC materials for energy storage and CO 2 capture via a single-step KOH activation approach, allowing for direct comparison and correlation of precursor chemistry. Furthermore, this provides a solid basis for future precursor-specific tuning of KOH loading, activation temperature and time, pore structure, and surface functioning to optimize properties and performance. Based on the motivating results for AC3, the electrochemical performance of the AC3-based symmetric full-cell in 2 M KOH was then determined using cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic charge−discharge, rate capability, and cycle stability evaluations. In Figure 8a, the cyclic voltammograms recorded in the po- tential window of 0.0−0.8 V at scan rates from 5 to 100 mV s −1 show a relatively symmetric quasi-rectangular/leaf-like shape with no distinct redox peaks, as also observed in the case of the half-cell, indicating that the charge-storage mechanism is pri- marily electric double-layer capacitive. The gradual increase in current response with scan rate, as well as the preservation of the overall CV shape, indicate good electrochemical reversibility and an adequate rate respo

ally the narrower micropores. Yet, the device retains ∼70% of its initial capaci- tance despite a 4-fold increase in current density, demonstrating a reasonable rate capability for a symmetric AC full cell. Figure 8d shows that capacitance retention first decreases somewhat before restoring to ∼100% during the initial stages of cycling, which can be attributed to gradual electrolyte wetting and ac- tivation of the porous electrode structure. Following initial stabilization, the capacitance gradually drops with further cy- cling, reaching ∼78% retention after 1000 cycles, indicating moderate long-term stability of the symmetric cell. Yet, the gradual reduction indicates electrode−electrolyte interface de- terioration or a partial loss of accessible electroactive surface area upon multiple charge−discharge cycles. An indication that supports the efforts required to achieve enhanced cyclic stability by post-modifications of AC employing advanced techniques. While the current work shows the potential of agro-food industrial biowaste-derived AC for electrochemical energy storage and CO 2 capture applications, some elements of practical implementation deserve additional exploration. The synthesis procedure uses easily accessible agro-industrial bio- waste feedstocks and well-established, intrinsically scalable carbonization and activation techniques, yet a thorough techno- economic analysis is outside the domain of this work and has to be investigated in future studies. Long-term electrochemical cycling stability, in particular, is a significant criterion for evaluating electrode durability and capacitance retention over extended periods of operation, and efforts should be made to achieve and sustain it. At the same time, dynamic breakthrough experiments based on mixed-gas adsorption measurements has to be carried out to determine selectivity in real-world scenarios. Future research should systematically assess improving per- formance and cycling stability, cost-effectiveness, process scal- ability, and energy requirements to provide a more thorough assessment of the long-term applicability of these materials by implementing advanced modification strategies that closely adhere to sustainable options. 4. The combination of micropores and mesopores yielding a hi- erarchical pore morphology, as well as the presence of functional groups at the pores had a significant influence on CO 2 ad- sorption and selectivity. AC2 exhibited the highest capture capacity of 2.55 mmol/g at 298 K and 1 bar along with cyclic stability, as well as an experimental CO 2 /N 2 selectivity of 46.5 at 50 mbar, indicating that selective CO 2 adsorption is primarily controlled by the availability of energetically favorable ad- sorption sites, whereas the pressure-dependent selectivity be- havior indicates progressive active sites occupation. The dominance of physisorption-induced CO 2 affinity is indicated by an increase in adsorption capacity of 2.82 mmol/g for AC2 at 273 K, with low Q st values in the 13.8−7 kJ/mol range and stability over multiple cycles. Electrochemical measurements reveal that the high graphitic carbon content and resulting electrical conductivity, accessible hierarchical pore structure with high microporosity, and oxygen-containing surface func- tionalities of the AC samples are the primary contributors for the high capacitive response across the investigated scan rate range, which is consistent with enhanced ion transport and stable electric double-layer formation. The AC3 half-cell system ex- hibited the lowest solution and charge-transfer resistance, as well as the large

ic capacitance of ∼250 F/g at a 5 mV/s scan rate. At the same time, symmetric full-cell system-based GCD profiles exhibited almost symmetric charge−discharge curves with a reasonable rate capability, retaining ∼70% of initial ca- pacitance despite a 4-fold increase in current density and ∼78% retention of capacitance after 1000 cycles. AC produced from agro-industrial waste streams is therefore promising in selective CO 2 capture and supercapacitors coupling potential in- environmental and energy applications with waste upcycling. In summary, the dual performance of these AC samples is de- termined by the interplay of graphitization, surface functionality, and pore structure. A hierarchical pore structure with surface functional groups promotes CO 2 affinity, while a hierarchical pore network with increased graphitic ordering promotes ion transport and hence electrochemical charge storage. Balancing these structural elements is thus critical for optimal performance in CO 2 capture and supercapacitor applications. The evidenced results also suggest that future research should focus on dynamic breakthrough experiments based on mixed-gas adsorption measurements to determine selectivity under practical condi- tions, as well as asymmetric two-electrode supercapacitor testing to determine true device-level performance in terms of energy density, power density, and long-term cycling stability. ■ AUTHOR INFORMATION Corresponding Authors Suresh Kuppireddy − Renewable and Sustainable Energy Research Center, Technology Innovation Institute (TII), Abu Dhabi 9639, United Arab Emirates; � orcid.org/0000- 0003-0956-6521; Email: suresh.kuppireddy@tii.ae Georgios N. Among various energy-storage sys- tems, rechargeable batteries generally provide relatively high energy density, whereas electrochemical capacitors, particularly supercapacitors, have attracted considerable attention because of their high power density, rapid charge–discharge capability, long cycling life, and operational safety [ 1–8 ]. Recent advances in graphene-based and flexible electrochemical energy-storage systems have further demonstrated the importance of elec- trode architecture, surface chemistry, and electrode–electrolyte interactions in determining energy-storage performance [ 9–11 ]. Carbon materials have been widely investigated as supercapac- itor electrodes because of their physicochemical stability, large specific surface area, favorable charge-transport characteristics, and tunable pore architecture [ 12–18 ]. The CSK-750-2 symmetric supercapacitor achieved an energy density of 10.5 Wh kg− 1 at a power density of 500 W kg− 1 and maintained 7.9 Wh kg− 1 at 5000 W kg− 1 , together with approximately 106% capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles. hits.text: N The global demand for high-performance, environmentally friendly, and efficient energy storage systems continues to rise in line with the rapid advancement of modern technologies. Among various options, supercapacitors have attracted significant attention due to their density, rapid charge− discharge capability, and excellent cycling stability compared to conventional batteries. 1−5 However, their relatively low energy density remains a limitation. 6 Consequently, the development of advanced electrode materials capable of simultaneously delivering high capacitance and long-term stability has become a research focus. In this context, transition metal oxides and porous carbon materials are emerging as promising candidates, as they offer complementary charge- storage pseudocapacitance and electric double-layer capaci- tance (EDLC) mechanisms, respectively. 7−9 Supercapacitors generally store energy through two primary mechanisms, EDLC and pseudocapacitance. In EDLC systems, charge storage occurs through the electrostatic accumulation of electrolyte ions at the electrode/electrolyte interface without involving faradaic reactions, enabling excellent power capability and long-term cycling stability. 10,11 Porous carbon materials, including activated carbon, graphene, and biomass-derived carbon, are widely utilized as EDLC electrodes due to their high electrical conductivity, large accessible surface area, and hierarchical pore structures. In contrast, pseudocapacitive materials store charge through rapid and reversible faradaic reactions involving surface redox processes, providing higher specific capacitance than conventional carbon-based electro- des. Transition metal oxides have attracted considerable attention as pseudocapacitive materials because of their multiple oxidation states and rich redox activity. However, their practical applications are often limited by poor electrical conductivity and structural instability during repeated charge− discharge cycles. 12 Therefore, integrating transition metal oxides with porous carbon materials represents an effective strategy to combine the high capacitance contribution of Received: May 29, 2026 Revised: August 4, 2026 Accepted: September 2, 2026 Published: September 24, 2026 Articlepubs.acs.org/EF © 2026 American Chemical Society 22237 https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.energyfuels.6c02824 Energy Fuels 2026, 40, 22237−22254 Downloaded from pubs.​acs.​org/​enfuem/​article-pdf/​40/​40/​22237/​68635917/​acs.​energyfuels.​6c02824.​pdf by ZHEJIANG UNIV user on 16 O

The combination of EFB-derived activated carbon with Fe-doped ZnO to simultaneously exploit the high electrical conductivity and large surface area of biomass-derived carbon together with the enhanced pseudo- capacitive activity

The results demonstrate that the synergistic effects of Fe doping and ZnO-carbon hybridization with a locally abundant, waste-derived carbon matrix significantly enhance the redox activity, electrical conductivity, and cycling durability. Distinct from previous studies, this work integrates Fe doping and ZnO-carbon hybridization within an EFB-based activated carbon matrix, achieving improved electrochemical perform- ance through a fully biomass-supported material architecture. This integrated approach offers an effective and sustainable material design approach for the development of high- performance materials with enhanced electrochemical proper- ties for advanced energy-storage applications. 2. The durability results demon- strated that the asymmetric coin cell based on 25%-Fe-ZnO/ AC exhibited superior cycling stability compared with the 4%- Fe-ZnO/AC, 15%-Fe-ZnO/AC, and 8%-Fe-ZnO/AC cells. The accumulated mechanical stress over thousands of cycles can induce structural fatigue, including partial pulverization of the nanoparticles and weakening of their attachment to the activated carbon matrix. Consequently, the deterioration of interparticle contact and conductive pathways contributes to the increased ESR observed after cycling. In contrast, the relatively stable and slightly decreased R ct after prolonged cycling highlights the importance of the Fe−C interfacial interaction in maintaining charge-transfer kinetics. The strong covalent Fe−C anchoring bonds effectively preserve intimate contact between the Fe-containing active species and the conductive carbon framework, preventing severe interfacial separation and maintaining accessible electron-transfer pathways during repeated cycling. Therefore, although some structural degradation occurs within the pseudocapacitive component, the stabilized interface helps prevent catastrophic electrode failure and preserves electro- chemical reversibility. Similar roles of metal−carbon interfacial interactions in improving structural stability and charge- transfer behavior have been reported for advanced composite electrodes. 53 The capacitance retention of 72% after long-term cycling (Figure 9e) therefore results from the combined effects of gradual degradation of Fe-doped ZnO, partial loss of electrochemically active sites, and increased internal resist- ance. 59 The FESEM images after the durability test further support this interpretation (Figure S3). Despite the noticeable capacitance decay, the Coulombic efficiency remained remarkably high at 99.9%, indicating a highly reversible and stable charge−discharge process through- out the cycling test. Under the 45° bending condition, the electrochemical durability exhibited faster performance degra- dation compared to the initial state. The capacitance retention decreased to 56.5% after 1500 cycles and further dropped to 15.2% after 3000 cycles, while the Coulombic efficiency remained at 100% (Figure 11f). These results suggest that mechanical deformation induced by bending adversely affected the electrochemical stability of the flexible ASC device, leading to accelerated capacitance fading during prolonged cycling. Compared with recently reported flexible supercapacitors, the electrochemical performance of the present flexible ASC is within the range reported for biomass- and ZnO/carbon-based flexible energy storage devices, although its cycling stability remains relatively lower. Huang et al. reported a flexible NCNF/BC@ZnO/NiCo-LDH asymmetric supercapacitor with an energy density of 21 Wh kg −1 at a power density of 757.1 W kg −1 and 80% capacitance retention after 8000 cycles. 64 A coffee waste-derived activated carbon-based flexible supercapacitor delivered an energy density of 12.5 Wh kg −1 at a power density of 202 W kg −1 , while maintaining 90.5% capacitance retention after 5000 cycles, 65 a flexible Co- (OH) 2 //porous carbon asymmetric supercapacitor also exhibited a high energy density of 76.7 Wh kg −1 at 1416.9 W kg −1 together with 91% capacitance retention after 5000 cycles, 66 and a RuO 2 /CNOs flexible supercapacitor delivered an energy density of 10.6 Wh kg −1 at a power density of 4456 kW kg −1 while maintaining 94.47% capacitance retention after 4000 cycles. 67 In comparison, the present Fe-ZnO/AC-based flexible ASC achieved a comparable energy density of 20.5 Wh kg −1 at 240.4 W kg −1 but showed lower cycling stability, retaining 55.7% of its initial capacitance after 5000 cycles. The relatively faster capacitance decay may be attributed to gradual electrochemical degradation of the active material, possible structural instability, and interfacial deterioration between the electrode, electrolyte, and current collector during prolonged cycling 64 rather than mechanical deformation, since the cycling test was conducted in the initial state before bending. EIS analysis revealed an overall increase in impedance after bending, associated with higher charge-transfer resistance and hindered ion transport due to mechanical strain. Interestingly, the ESR in the after-bending state was slightly lower than that in the initial state (Figure 11i), possibly due to improved interfacial contact induced by mechanical compression during bending. In this study, an integrated recycling strategy is developed to utilize the organic and metallic components collected from used heated tobacco as active materials and current collectors for an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) . Residual t obacco leaves are carbonized to obtain carbonized tobacco leaves (CTL), while metallic heating elements (MHEs) are directly reused without melting, reshaping, or additional processing. The MHEs maintain their morphology , surface characteristics, and electrical continuity after tobacco use . A CTL-based slurry is coated onto the MHE to fabricate th

mmetric supercapacitor device assembled by M15 -CTL/MHE and CTL/MHE operates stably over 0–2.0 V and exhibits a gravimetric specific capacitance of 39.2 F g−1 at 1 A g −1. The device further achieves a maximum energy density of 23.6 Wh kg−1 and a power density of 10.0 kW kg−1, retains 81.8% of its initial capacitance after 3000 cycles, and successfully illuminates a 1.8 V red light-emitting diode. These results demonstrate the direct integration of multiple components from a single waste product into functional energy storage device. 1. Introduction The rapid expansion of renewable energy systems, electric vehicles, and large -scale artificial intelligence data centers has increased the demand for efficient energy storage systems [1–3]. Among the available technologies, supercapacitors have attracted considerable attention owing to their rapid charge–discharge capability, h

paration of a carbon active material. The active material must be combined with a mechanically stable and electrically conductive current collector , while a complete device requires positive and negative electrodes with complementary electrochemical characteristics and an ion-conducting electrolyte [22, 23]. Numerous biomass-recycling studies have focused mainly on converting a single organic fraction into an electrode material while continuing to rely on commercially available current collectors [24–26]. Such approach es demonstrate the applicability of biomass -derived carbon but do not fully utilize the functional components already present in heterogeneous waste products. Therefore, a broader recycling strategy should separate the physically and chemically distinct waste fractions of the original product and assign each fraction a suitable role within the energy storage device. Despite its suitability as a carbon electrode, biomass -derived carbon stores charge through a predominantly non-Faradaic mechanism, which can limit capacitance and energy density [27]. Pseudocapacitive transition metal oxides can compensate for this limitation by providing additional charge storage through reversible redox reactions [8, 11]. Among them, manganese dio

ns, cellulose -acetate or PLA -based filter components, and aluminum -coated paper obtained from heated tobacco waste [3 7, 38]. However, the direct reuse of an MHE as the current collector for both electrodes, together with tobacco -leaf-derived carbon from the same waste product, remains largely unexplored. In this study, a recycling strategy was developed to recover both tobacco residues and metallic heating elements (MHEs) from used heated tobacco and integrate them into a single asymmetric supercapacitor device. These findings highlight the robustness of traditional KOH activation and hydrothermal approaches for generating stable electrode architectures, even when specific capacitance values are lower. Finally, oil palm em pty fruit bunch fibres provide an example of an environmentally favourable “binderless” activation pathway. Although quantitative metrics are less well defined, the reported capacitance exceeds that of commercial activated carbon, with improved cycling sta bility, demonstrating that green processing routes can yield electrodes that are competitive with conventional activation methods. Collectively, the comparison underscores a trade -off between maximizing specific capacitance and ensuring long -term cycling stability, with material selection and activation strategy being decisive factors. Nitrogen -doped bamboo-derived carbons clearly push the limits of capacitance, while more conventional precursors such as ginseng and walnut shells offer superior cycle life. This suggests that future research should emphasize integrating heteroatom doping or hierarchical porosity with processing routes that sustain stability over extended operation, thereby bridging the gap between high energy density and device reliability. Conclusion In this study, a sustainable and high-performance electrode material was successfully developed from bamboo stem biomass using NaOH chemical activation. The resulting carbon featured a hierarchical pore str

s, and partial graphitic ordering. These features enabled a hybrid charge storage mechanism, combining electric double-layer capacitance and pseudocapacitance. Electrochemical evaluation demonstrated a remarkably high specific capacitance of 833 F/g at 0.5 A/g, excellent rate capability, and 94% capacitance retention after 5000 cycles, highlighting the material’s robust stability and energy storage potential. The low equivalent series resistance (0.2 Ω) further validated the material’s high conductivity and fast ion diffusion pathways. Compared with other recently reported biomass-derived carbons, the bamboo-derived electrode material outperforms in terms of both capacitance and sustainability. This work demonstrates that bamboo stem, an abundant and renewable biomass resource, can serve as an effective prec ursor for producing activated carbon with tunable porosity and functional chemistry. The green synthesis route, combined with scalable processing, positions this material as a promising candidate for next-generation eco-friendly supercapacitor devices. Although the bamboo-derived activated carbon demonstrated high specific capacitance and excellent short-term cycling stability, the study is limited by the narrow aqueous voltage window and absence of long-term or large-scale evaluation. Future work will focu s on optimizing the activation process and expanding the voltage window through alternative electrolytes.

This review systematically evaluates heteroatom doping, nanocomposite engineering, and multi-element co- doping strategies within a unified structural electrochemical perfor - mance framework. Heteroatom doping primarily improves electronic conductivity and surface redox activity, while nanocomposite integration amplifies pseudocapacitive contributions and structural stability. Several critical factors, including capacitance, resis- tance, power density, energy density, cell potential and voltage, cycling life, equivalent series resistance, charge-discharge rate, and thermal stability, influence their overall performance and efficiency. Cycle Life The overall performance of a supercapacitor also depends on the stability of the device, which is a crucial parameter. This stability can be estimated by evaluating the life cycle using CV and GCD responses. Carbon materials are among the most capable electrode constituents for supercapacitors due to their excellent cycling stability; this is because their charge storage mechanism is highly reversible and involves physical adsorption and desorption processes. In contrast, pseudocapacitive elec- trode materials exhibit poor cyclic stability as chemical processes decrease the material’s reversibility. The cyclic performance of a supercapacitor is influenced by the choice of electrode materials and electrolytes, the operating voltage, the working temperature, and the frequency of charging and discharging cycles. 3.5. ESR represents the sum of the intrinsic resistances of the electrode materials and the electrolyte. Dif- ferent electrolytes have varying OPWs and ionic conductivities, influencing the ESR and, consequently, the power performance. Metal Oxide Nanomaterials Decorated BDC for Supercapacitor Application Metal oxide nanomaterial-decorated BDC is used as an electrode that is substantial for supercapacitors. They have higher specific capacitance than EDLC-type supercapacitors with high energy density. Generally, metal-based nanomaterials are mainly used as cathodes for energy storage devices, whereas the BDC are used as anodes in the supercapacitors. Metal oxide NPs are very suitable for electrode materials for supercapacitors. This is due to their porous structure th

ns. Such as owing to only EDLC behavior, they show a lower value of energy. Very small pore sizes are often electrochemically inaccessible to various ions, lowering the performance. Electrochemical supercapacitors are modern, newly developed, sustainable energy conversion and storage devices with numer- ous applications. High power density, long capacitance retention (cyclic stability), low cost, and environmental friendliness make them robust alternatives to batteries, fuel cells, and other conventional devices. However, supercapacitors have extremely lower specific energy compared to batteries, even though their power density is high. Another disadvantage of these devices is their working potential and cost, which can sometimes be higher than batteries. This work establishes a scalable electrode-design strategy for practical high-mass-loading ZIHCs. 1 Introduction The rapid expansion of electric vehicles, portable electronics, and grid-scale energy storage has intensified demand for electro- chemical energy storage systems that simultaneously deliver high energy and power densities, and long-term cycling stability [ 1–4 ]. Conventional metal-ion batteries, such as lithium-ion batteries, store energy via reversible Faradaic reactions but are limited by sluggish reaction kinetics and reduced capacity at high rates, which restricts their applicability in high-power applications [ 5– 7 ]. In contrast, electrochemical capacitors rely on interfacial ion adsorption/desorption processes, offering excellent power capa- bility and cycling durability, albeit at the expense of low energy density [ 8–10 ]. Hybrid ion capacitors have therefore emerged as a potential solution by integrating a battery-type anode with a capacitive cathode, achieving a favorable balance between energy density and power performance [ 11–13 ]. Among various hybrid systems, zinc-ion hybrid capacitors (ZIHCs), typically consisting of a metallic Zn anode and a carbon- based cathode, have attracted increasing attention. This interest stems from Zn’s high theoretical capacity (823 mAh g− 1 ), its low redox po

l freeze-drying. By correlating electrode structures, as characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and micro-computed tomography (micro-CT), with electrochemical performance, we show that long-range pore channels, combined with low electronic resis- tance, are critical for achieving high-rate capability and long- term cycling stability. An optimized ZIHC pouch cell with a low negative-to-positive electrode capacity (N/P) ratio of 16.4 delivers a high specific capacity of 38.3 mAh g− 1 at 10 A g− 1 over 3000 charge–discharge cycles with a device-level energy density of 2.82 Wh kg− 1 . This study provides useful insights into the relationship between cathode carbon material mass load- ing and electrochemical performance. 442 新 能 源 进 展 第 14 卷 2.1 分级多孔结构的构建 生物质炭的分级多孔结构可以有效提升 SSA 并 优化孔结构， 高SSA 可增加电极与电解液的接触面 积，提升电荷容量[47]。孔结构与材料导电性高度相 关，微孔在增加活性位点密度的同时，可能会限制 离子扩散；介孔可以促进电解液离子快速传输，提 升倍率性能；大孔可作为离子缓冲池，有效减少长 程扩散阻力。但在碳化过程中，过度发达的孔隙结 构会阻碍石墨微晶的生长（如 sp 2 杂化碳层减少）， 而石墨微晶是生物质炭导电性的主要来源，导电性 不足易引发极化效应，导致有效电容和循环寿命降 低[48-49]。除化学活化外，生物质炭分级多孔结构的 构建还可采用模板法和微波合成法等。WEI 等[32]以 玉米棒为碳源、KOH 为活化剂， 通过化学活化法制 备的分级活性炭（hierarchical activated charcoal-corn cob, HAC-CC ）具有 3D 多孔结构和较宽的孔径分 布，表现出大孔和中孔的互联网络结构。HAC-CC 的 SSA 为 1 104 m2/g，总孔体积为 0.718 cm3/g，平均孔 径为 2.497 nm。在 0.1 A/g 电流密度下，HAC-CC 的 比电容为 121 F/g，经 过2 500 次循环后， 仍具有88% 的电容保持率。LIU 等[38]以废棕榈为碳源， 通过微波 法制备的分级多孔炭（porous carbon, PC）具有不规 则的大孔、 中孔和微孔结构， 并具有互连的通道， 呈 现出无序的蠕虫状孔结构。PC 的 SSA 为 1 573 m 2/g， 总孔体积为 0.573 cm3/g。在0.5 A/g 电流密度下，PC 的比电容为 226 F/g ，2 000 次循环后仍具有 96.7% 的电容保持率。 HOU 等[50]以明胶为生物质前体， ZnCl2 为模板剂和活化剂，通过模板法制备了 SSA 为 1 336 m 2/g、总孔体积为 0.76 cm 3/g、平均孔径为 0.72 nm 的分级多孔炭 ZIGC，其孔结构以微孔为主。 ZnCl2 在活化期间产生 Cl2 和 CO2 在碳基质扩散， 产 生丰富且均匀的珊瑚状孔结构。 在0.5 A/g 电流密度 下，ZIGC 的比电容为 337.6 F/g。表3 总结了化学活 化法、微波法和模板法合成的优缺点。 表 3 分级多孔炭构建工艺对比 Table 3 Comparison of graded porous carbon construction processes 构建方法 条件 优点 缺点 参考文献 化学活化法 以 KOH 为活化剂，在 800 ℃下活化 60 min 制备工艺简单；具有高比表 面积和孔隙率，结构可调性 强，是常用的方法 一般需在强酸强碱条件下进行，易 造成环境污染；高温活化过程中结 构易坍塌 [32] 模板法 以 ZnCl2 为模板， 在3 ℃ 下交联胶凝化 60 min，冷 冻干燥 24 h ；随后在 800 ℃下保温 60 min 可精准设计微孔、介孔结构， 利于离子扩散，循环稳定性 好；一般无需强腐蚀性试剂， 环境友好 制备步骤繁琐，产率较低，工业化难 度大；模板可能导致孔道孤立，影响 离子传输效率 [50] 微波法 在 500 ℃下保温 2 h ，随 后在微波炉中以 700 W 功率加热 5 min 微波加热速率快，能耗小；具 有较高比表面积和孔隙率 设备成本较高， 不适合大规模生产； 需选择高介电损耗的生物质或添加 微波吸收剂，普适性受限；快速加热 导致局部过热、孔隙均匀性较差 [38] 2.2 表面官能团改性 通过引入或调控生物质炭表面含氧、含氮等官 能团，可显著优化其表面化学性质和电子结构，有 效提升其储能性能。氧化处理通常用于在活性炭表 面添加含氧官能团，以增加其表面湿润性和导电性。 LENG 等 [51]以椰子壳为碳源，H2O2 为氧化剂，通过 碳化法制备的炭材料氧元素占比从 8.97%增加到 16.09%，在0.1 A/g 电流密度下， 复合材料的比电容 从 296 F/g 增加到 487 F/g 。碳量子点从表面释放到 液相中，与氧自由基结合形成氧化的碳量子点，稳 定的氧基团和化学键结合在碳骨架中，赋予其优异 的导电性。但生物质炭表面官能团改性存在工艺复 杂、污染环境、在高温或长期使用中易分解、性能提 升较小等问题。因此，目前对生物质炭表

掺杂可以发挥协同增强作用，因此，目前研究多采 用多种杂原子共掺杂策略。 2.4 赝电容材料协同效应 赝电容储能机理主要依赖于电极材料表面的快 速氧化还原反应，而基于 EDLC 与赝电容协同作用 机制构筑的混合电容器，将过渡金属化合物或导电 聚合物（如聚苯胺）锚定于生物炭表面，结合了物理 吸附和快速氧化还原反应的协同作用，显著提高了 材料的电化学性能，赝电容结构和混合电容器的机 理如图 3 所示。然而，过渡金属化合物纳米材料在 循环过程中的体积膨胀会导致容量急剧衰减，而杂 原子作为活性位点，可以促进 TMO 表面反应动力 学， 形成 “双活性中心” 机制； 生物炭载体孔隙结构 与杂原子位点共同形成“纳米反应器”，可以限制 TMO 颗粒尺寸，抑制 TMO 体积膨胀；同时，杂原 子提供孤对电子或改变载体导电性， 优化TMO 的电 子传导路径，并通过静电作用抑制TMO 溶解，从而 增强其循环稳定性 [56]。TAN 等[57]采用模板法在碳纳 米片 （carbon nanosheets, CNSs） 上配位铋原子制备了 Bi-N3S1，在 0.2 A/g 电流密度下，具有447.9 mA·h/g 的高比电容，经过 5 000 次循环后，电容保持率为 73.61%。Bi-N3S1 中的 Bi 原子与 3 个 N 原子和 1 个 S 原子配位，形成的高度不对称配位构型使电子重 排和畸变，增强了中心 Bi 活性位和 K+ 吸附能力， 实现了高电容贡献率和较好的电化学性能。炭材料 稳定的框架结构也可以有效减少过渡金属纳米材料 的体积膨胀。 JI 等 [55]将 N、O、P 掺杂的多孔炭 （NOPC）与 CoCl2 混合，通过水热法将 Co3O4 纳米 片垂直锚定在 NOPC 表面，制备的 Co3O4NS@NOPC 复合材料在 1 A/g 电流密度下具有 659.7 F/g 的比电 容，组装的水性 SC 在 746 W/kg 功率密度下，表现 出 42.5 W·h/kg 的能量密度。 多杂原子掺杂可以降低 电阻、提高电导率，而层状 Co3O4 提供了高能量密 度和电荷转移效率，Co3O4 与 NOPC 的协同作用显 著提高了电化学性能。王永妮[58]以柚子皮为碳源制 备了生物质多孔炭（biomass porous carbon, BPC）， 并将其与硝酸镍和硝酸钴混合，通过水热法和热解 法制备了 NiCo2O4@BPC/NF 复合材料，在 1 A/g 电 流密度下，BPC、NiCo2O4/NF 和 NiCo2O4@BPC/NF 的比电容分别为 240.67、252.56 和 392.2 F/g ，经过 3 000 次循环后电容保持率分别为 100%、80.19%和 93.51%。生物质炭的三维导电网络不仅为赝电容反 应提供了电子快速传输通道，还通过物理约束缓冲 了 TMO 在充放电过程中的体积膨胀，从而提升循 环稳定性，且高分散的 TMO 纳米颗粒通过增大有 效反应界面，增强了赝电容效应。CHEN 等[59]通过 金属有机骨架热解和原位硒化技术，将 Bi/Bi3Se4 纳 米颗粒封装在碳纳米棒（ carbon nanorod, CNR ）中 制备了 Bi/Bi3Se4@CNR，在 1 A/g 电流密度下循环 400 次后仍具有 322.9 mA·h/g 的比电容和 89%的容 量保持率。Bi 基 MOF 结构具有较大的直径，但由 于多孔炭框架的物理隔离作用有助于控制 Bi 基合 金化合物的尺寸，生成的 Bi/Bi3Se4 杂化颗粒基本上 为纳米尺寸，且 Bi/Bi3Se4 与多孔炭框架之间的紧密 连接， 有效减少了金属团聚现象， 抑制充放电过程 中金属纳米颗粒的体积膨胀， 显著提升复合材料的 444 新 能 源 进 展 第 14 卷 综上所述，生物质材料可以通过构建分级多孔 结构调节孔隙结构与石墨化程度以获得更大的比容 量和更强的导电性； 通过含氧、 含氮等官能团改性， 优化其表面化学性质和电子结构，有效提升其储能 性能；使用不同杂原子掺杂可有效改善材料的分级 孔结构、 氧化还原活性和润湿性等性能； 引入TMO 可激发生物质炭与 TMO 的协同效应，显著提升生 物质炭/TMO 材料的电化学性能。 3 典型生物质炭/TMO 复合体系的构 建及储能特性 目前 TMO 的研究主要聚焦于锰基氧化物 （MnOx）、 镍钴基氧化物和铁基氧化物。 作为典型的 赝电容材料，TMO 的多重氧化态特性赋予其优异的 氧化还原活性和高理论电容，但因其孔隙率较低且 循环过程中易发生结构损伤，导致离子传输迟滞且 循环稳定性下降，严重制约了实际应用。因此，通过 构筑 TMO 与生物质炭基体的复合结构，不仅能充 分发挥生物质炭材料高比表面积和导电性对 TMO 赝电容反应的促进作用，还能利用 TMO 的高理论 容量弥补生物质炭材料的低电容缺陷，实现性能协 同增效。 3.1 生物质炭/锰基氧化物复合体系 MnOx 凭借其多重氧化态转换特性、高比电容、 环境友好性及丰富的自然储量等优势，被视为极具 发展潜力的赝电容材料体系。 3.1.1 生物质炭/MnO2 复合材料 MnO2 因其独特的层状/隧道结构可实现快速的 Mn2+/Mn3+ 多价态转换，使其具有较宽的电化学稳 定窗口和高理论比容量[60]。但 MnO2 因导电率低， 且在充放电过程中易发生结构坍塌，导致电荷传输 迟滞，使其循环稳定性较差且实际比容量显著低于 理论值。WANG 等[61]以茄子皮为原料，采用一步碳 化法制备茄子炭（ Eggplant charcoal, EC ），并以 KMnO4 为氧化剂， 采用原位水热晶化法将海胆状结 构的 MnO2 负载到 EC 表面，制备了 MnO2/EC 复合 材料。MnO2/EC 在 0.5 A/g 的电流密度下的比电容 为 652.5 F/g，在 10 000 次循环后表现出 79.2%的电 容保持率。MnO2 提供更高赝电容，EC 增强整体电 导率，两者的协同效应使其具有优异的电容性能。 LI 等 [62]以含油污泥废弃物为碳源、 KMnO4 为氧化 剂，采用可控原位化学共沉淀法制备的巢状 MnO2 纳 米线/多级孔炭复合材料，在 0.5 A/g 电流密度下的 比电容为 437.9 F/g，经过 5 000 次循环后电容保持率 为 78.5%。以该分级多孔炭（hierarchical porous carbon, HPC）为负极组装的不对称SC，在 498.8 W/kg 功率 密度下，具有 59.67 W·h/kg 的能量密度。如图 4 所 示，HNO3 预氧化使多孔炭表面产生丰富的羧基和羟 基，这些含氧官能团在溶液中呈酸性，增强了 KMnO 4 的氧化程度，同时可使 MnO2 与基底生物质 炭表面化学键结合更强，MnO2 纳米线进一步生长、 聚集并组装成 3D 巢状结构，显著增加反应活性位 点，提高了复合材料的电化学性能。WANG 等[63]以 KMnO4 为锰源， 利用水热法在竹浆纤维多孔炭微球 表面合成了 MnO2，在 0.5 A/g 的电流密度下，具有 364.4 F/g 的比电容，在 10 000 次循环后仍具有 99.7% 的电容保持率，制备的对称超级电容器在 164 W/kg 的功率密度下， 具有12.6 W·h/kg 的能量密度。 纳米 片状 MnO2 提高了电子导电性、降低了内阻，竹浆 纤维多孔炭的分级多孔结构有利于离子和电荷的快 速转移，从而促进 MnO 2 纳米片在 KOH 电解质中的 氧化还原反应，二者协同作用使多孔炭球的电容性 能提高了 81%。 图 4 生物质炭预碳化及分级多孔炭和 MnO2 复合过程的结构示意图[62] Fig. 4 Schematic representation of the structure of biomass ch arcoal during precarbonization and composite process of graded porous carbon and MnO2[62]

塞部分微孔， 导致比表面积减小， 阻碍 电子传输。 KIM 等 [65] 利用飞秒激光直写技术 （femtosecond laser direct writing technology, FsLDW） 在木质激光诱导石墨烯（ laser-induced graphene, LIG）上嵌入 MnO，实现了绿色微超级电容器的制 备。如图 6 所示，通过 FsLDW 分别将木材和高锰酸 盐转化为 LIG 和 MnO，在木材上直接合成 MnO/LIG 异质纳米结构，在 10 mV/s 扫描速率下表现出 35.54 mF/cm2 高面电容。制备的 SC 在 80 µW/cm2 的 功率密度下， 具有0.67 µW·h/cm2 的能量密度， 经过 10 000 次循环后电容保持率约为 82.31%，具有稳定 性高、成本低和制备工艺简单的特点。WANG 等[66] 通过超富集和碳化处理，制备了一种新型的MnO 修 饰的人厌槐叶萍基多孔炭（SAC-MnO）复合材料，在 1 A/g 的电流密度下，该材料具有 436.8 F/g 的比电 容。组装的对称超级电容器在功率密度为694.6 W/kg 时的能量密度为 9.573 W·h/kg，经 过1 000 次循环后 电容保持率为 94.7%。SAC-MnO 复合材料显示出分 级的微孔−介孔结构，有利于离子传输和能量存储， 且锰氧化物锚定在碳基质可以诱导产生赝电容效 应，使电极材料具有优异的电化学性能。 图 5 T G C 0（a）、TGC1（b）、TGC2（c）、TGC3（d）、 TGC4（e）的 SEM 图像[64] Fig. 5 SEM images of TGC0 (a), TGC1 (b), TGC2 (c), TGC3 (d), and TGC4 (e)[64] 图 6 M n O / L I G异质纳米结构的制备工艺流程（a）及其应用（b）[65] Fig. 6 Preparation process flow (a) and applications (b) of MnO/LIG heterogeneous nanostructures[65] 综上所述，MnO2 通过 Mn2+/Mn3+ 多价态的转 换，使其理论容量高于 MnO，但其导电性较差且在 充放电过程中易发生结构坍塌；MnO 比 MnO2 结构 更加稳定且成本低廉，但其导电性和循环稳定性较 差，而引入生物质炭可以增强 MnOx 的导电性和循 环稳定性，提高复合材料的电化学性能。 3.2 生物质炭/镍钴基氧化物复合体系 在镍钴基氧化物中，二元（Co3O4、NiO）和三 元（NiCo2O4） 纳米材料由于其良好的电化学性能和 化学稳定性被广泛应用于赝电容电极材料。然而， 由于其导电性较差，且循环过程中体积膨胀导致容 量衰减等问题制约了其应用。因此，引入生物质炭

These attributes position EDLCs as a leading option among energy storage devices, particularly with respect to cyclic stability [ 48, 50]. PSCs function through a faradaic reduction–oxidation (redox) process, wherein charge storage is achieved by the reversible transfer of electrons between the electrode and the electrolyte, occurring at or near the electrode surface. In contrast to batteries, which rely on diffusion-controlled charge storage, PSCs undertake a surface-controlled mechanism. This distinction enables PSCs to attain higher energy densities compared to traditional EDLCs. The pseudocapacitive phenomenon is primarily observed in various materials, including m

oxide, as well as conductive polymers, including polyaniline and polypyrrole [50, 51]. HSCs integrate the charge storage mechanisms of both faradaic (pseudocapacitors) and non-faradaic (EDLCs) processes. By combining these two approaches, HSCs effec - tively balance performance parameters, offering a coordinated enhancement in cyclic stability, power density, and energy density. Such hybrid systems frequently utilize composite materials, often comprising carbon-based materials like graphene or carbon nanotubes intermixed with either conducting polymers or metal oxides, to optimize the electrochemical properties [48, 52]. The benchmark parameters for assessment of SC are- specific capacitance, cyclic sta - bility, equivalent series resistance (ESR), energy density (ED), and power density (PD) [53– 56]. Various electroanalytical techniques such as Electro Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS),

current collector, electrode, electrolyte, separator membrane) needs to be taken into consideration to evaluate the net resistance of SC cell, this is known as Equivalent Series Resistance (ESR). The EIS technique is utilized to calculate ESR, and is quantified in term of Ohm (Ω) and influenced by the type of electrolyte used. Cyclic stability is used to quantify SC’s performance after a certain number of cycles. It is mea- sured as difference between initial capacitance and the capacitance after n th consecu - tive cycle. It is commonly stated as % retention which is the degree of capacitance that is preserved. The capacitance decrement originates from several degradation processes such as electrode corrosion, redox byproduct buildup, active material loss, pore modi - fications, and increasing internal resistance. Cyclic stability reflects the extent to which an electrode material preserves its structural integrity and electrochemical functionality over repeated charge–discharge cycles.

The implementation of DESs in biomass fractionation encounters major obstacles, especially with solvent recycling, since this process remains essential for maintaining sustainable and affordable operations. The repeated use of recycled DES leads to hemicellulose degradation product accumulation, which negatively affects delignification effi - ciency throughout multiple cycles. The combination of hydrothermal pretreatment with DES application proves successful in maintaining delignification performance at high levels throughout at least five cycles because it reduces the negative effects of degradation byproducts. The preprocessing technique preserves solvent solvation properties, which results in steady fractionation outcomes ( Zhang et al., 2025b ). The purification of recycled DES is essential for enhancing its reus - ability and maintaining consistent performance in biomass processing. Activated carbon treatment has been shown to effectively remove im - purities and degradation products from recycled DES, restoring its original efficiency. This purification approach not only ensures the consistent quality of lignin and cellulose across processing cycles but also contributes to the operational reliability of DES in industrial ap - plications. The battery based on Fe-NSC 1000 showed no significant changes after 3,075 cycles, with a cycle life of up to 1025 h, which is considerably longer than the 100 h of the battery based on Pt/C. This demonstrates the high stability of the battery. Specifically, the zinc-air battery based on Fe-NSC 1000 exhibited a voltage gap of 0.9966 V and a cycling efficiency of 54.28% in the initial stage. After 700 h, the voltage gap became 1.0078 V, and the cycling efficiency was 53.14%. After 1,000 h, the voltage gap only increased slightly to 1.0386 V, and the cycling efficiency was 52.14%. This minor change further confirms its long-term stability and demon- strates its significant potential as a cathode material for ZABs. 73 To further evaluate the structural stability of Fe-NSC 1000, the SEM, XRD, and XPS were performed after the battery durability test. As shown in Figure S11, the SEM image of the Fe-NSC 1000 shows that the porous nanosheet-like morphology is largely retained, without obvious collapse of the carbon framework or severe aggregation. Because of the relatively low catalyst loading, the post-cycling catalyst-coated carbon-paper/Ni-foam air cathode was directly subjected to XRD characterization. Therefore, the sharp graphitic carbon, metallic Ni, and PTFE-related peaks mainly originate from the carbon paper, Ni-foam current collector, and PTFE-containing electrode component, respectively. As shown in the enlarged carbon diffraction region in the inset, a broad carbonaceous background is present underneath the intense carbon-paper reflection, consistent with the broad carbon peak of Fe-NSC 1000 being overlapped and largely obscured by the stronger substrate signal. Apart from the diffraction features associated with the electrode substrate and PTFE component, no additional resolvable peaks attributable to newly formed crystalline Fe-containing phases are observed after long-term cycling. In addition, the XPS spectra confirm that Fe-, N-, and S-containing species are still detectable after the durability test. Although slight changes in the relative proportions of surface species may occur, probably due to surface oxidation, electrolyte exposure, or partial surface reconstruction under alkaline conditions, the major chemical features of Fe-NSC 1000 are largely preserved. 74,75 These results demonstrate the good morphological and compositional stability of Fe-NSC 1000, which contributes to its durable Zn-air battery performance

However, the intermittent nature of these sources needs the use of efficient energy storage systems to ensure continuous power delivery and increase grid stability [4–7]. Supercapacitors are remarkable for their high-power density, quick charge/discharge ability, excellent cycling stability, and long service life, and several electrical energy storage technologies have garnered considerable attention [8–10]. These advantages make them particularly desirable for applications where the power delivery is instantaneous such as electric vehicles, portable gadgets, wearable devices and hybrid energy storage systems [2,11,12]. However, further research of improved electrode materials and optimized device architectures are required to increase the energy and power performance without affecting the long-term cycle stability to sustain efficient electrochemical performance at high current densities [13–15]. Supercapacitors are often categorized as electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs), pseudocapacitors and hybrid supercapacitors according to charge-storage mechanism [16–20]. EDLCs store charge via a non-faradaic process of ion adsorption and possess great power density and cycling stability, but have a restricted energy density. Pseudocapacitors, in contrast, use rapid and reversible faradaic reactions to obtain larger capacitance, whereas hybrid supercapacitors combine capacitive and battery-type electrodes to balance energy and power densities [18–20]. However, nonlinear electrochemical behaviour arising from the intricate interaction between electrode structure, electrolyte and operating circumstances makes performance optimization difficult [9,21]. Cobalt oxides (CoO, CoO) and cobalt-containing- layered oxides (e.g., LiCoO) are widely used in lithium-ion batteries due to their high theoretical capacities, stable cycling performance, and favourable redox behaviour. Nanoscale cobalt oxides offer enhanced lithium diffusion and improved structural stability during charge- discharge cycling. CoO nanostructures, such as nanowires, nanosheets, and hollow spheres, exhibit high reversible capacities and reduced volume expansion, making them promising anode materials [ , ]. Cobalt-based nanomaterials, particularly, CoO and Co(OH) exhibit excellent pseudocapacitive behaviour. Their redox-active surfaces enable rapid charge transfer and high speciﬁc capacitance. Nano structuring improves electrolyte accessibility and electron transport, leading to enhanced energy and power densities [ , , ]. Cobalt nanoparticles and cobalt nitrogen-dope

ystallinity [ ]. The integration of cobalt nanomaterials into practical devices presents additional challenges related to material compatibility, long-term reliability, and manufacturing constraints. For example, in energy storage systems, cobalt nanostructures must maintain structural integrity during repeated charge–discharge cycles and operate safely under varying temperatures and electrolytes [ ]. Despite current challenges, several emerging research directions offer exciting opportunities for advancing cobalt nanomaterials. Single-atom catalysts, where isolated cobalt atoms are dispersed on conductive supports such as graphene or nitrogen-doped carbon, have demonstrated exceptional catalytic efficiency due to maximum atom utilization and unique electronic structures [ ]. Another transformative direction is the application of machine learning in materials discovery and optimization [ ]. Coupling computational modelling with high-throughput experimentation is expected to signiﬁcantly reduce development time for next-generation materials. Emphasis on environmentally responsible production, recycling strategies, and cobalt-efficient materials will also be critical to ensure long-term technological and societal impact. 9.
